items.title: China's Latest A.I. Breakthrough Threatens America's Lead
items.desc: Chinese start-up Moonshot AI released Kimi K3, billed as the world's largest open-source model and benchmarked near the best U.S. systems, sending AI-chip stocks down about 1% and reviving doubts over whether U.S. hyperscalers' vast data-center spending is justified. [NYT, posted 2026-07-17]

items.title: Meta in Talks to Lease Computing Power to Anthropic in Potential $10 Billion Deal
items.desc: Meta is in early talks to rent out AI computing capacity to Anthropic for up to $10 billion over two years, a move that would open a new revenue line for Meta and underscores how scarce and expensive compute has become amid a data-center building boom. [NYT, posted 2026-07-17]

items.title: A.I. Is Running on Borrowed Money
items.desc: Big Tech's roughly $800 billion in 2026 AI data-center spending is increasingly financed by bonds, pushing Oracle's debt near junk status and prompting warnings that the capital-intensive AI buildout echoes the risks of the dot-com and railroad booms. [NYT, posted 2026-07-17]

items.title: America's Enterprising Spirit Is Booming After Decades-Long Slump
items.desc: New-business formation is surging in the U.S., ending a decades-long drought, with entrepreneurs increasingly using AI tools to launch and run companies faster and more cheaply. [NYT, posted 2026-07-17]

items.title: How Data Centers Became a Symbol of Americans' Rage
items.desc: The AI-driven data-center boom is fueling local backlash over water use, secrecy, and community costs, with projects like Google's planned Oklahoma facility becoming flashpoints for broader frustration with Big Tech's expansion. [Washington Post, posted 2026-07-18]
